88334d994f1ecabe: This chunk opens the LICN-001 General License Requirements policy, stating the policy objective of the State Board of Education to staff North Carolina public schools with qualified teachers, administrators, and student services personnel, and delegates licensure administration authority from the State Board of Education to the Superintendent of Public Instruction and, in turn, to DPI staff. df6cf441b48a3204: This chunk, part of the LICN-001 General License Requirements within the LICN Policy Series, defines "clear license" (the conditions a professional educator license must meet to be in good standing, free of pending or imposed discipline, and not surrendered under investigation) and "continuing education unit" (CEU, the credit earned by professional educators toward license renewal, equal to two-thirds of a semester credit hour or ten clock hours of professional development). fbab3fb3c64bf0bb: This chunk is part of the definitions section (LICN-001 §2) of the General License Requirements policy, defining the professional educator license types and terms used across the LICN Policy Series, including the Continuing Professional License (CPL), Initial Professional License (IPL), and Emergency License (EL), as well as "jurisdiction," "license," and "EVAAS." 922429f3dac0b8fb: This chunk supplies definitions from LICN-001 §2 for license area, licensure examination requirements, lifetime license, limited license, and out-of-state applicant, which govern how North Carolina professional educator licenses are classified and who qualifies for them. a15817bc88e6e902: This chunk contains definitions from LICN-001 §2 (General License Requirements) for the LICN Policy Series, covering out-of-state exams, professional educator categories, provisional assistant principal and residency licenses, the renewal cycle for continuing professional licenses, and the State Salary Schedule. b73c16c55715759c: This chunk supplies three definitions from LICN-001 §2 (Definitions) that govern the professional educator licensure series: "student services personnel" (including school counselors, social workers, psychologists, audiologists, speech-language pathologists, and media coordinators), the "student services personnel license" issued under LICN-012, and "teacher" as an individual whose major responsibility is teaching or directly supervising teaching. 2e464a373d760ba2: This chunk, Section 3 of LICN-001 (General License Requirements), sets out the baseline licensure rules for professional educators in North Carolina public schools: who must hold a DPI-issued license (Teacher, Administrator, or Student Services Personnel), what information each license must show, and that any educator preparation program a license requires must be recognized by the SBE or the equivalent out-of-state licensing authority.
c92900de19c15341: This chunk, within LICN-001 (General License Requirements), sets out when DPI must issue a professional educator license and what makes a license application complete, including submission of required documents under LICN-004, payment of the fee under LICN-008, and clearance of any Superintendent investigation under LICN-007. 28ef7c49ed51b9c9: This provision, LICN-001 §3(g) in the General License Requirements of the North Carolina LICN Policy Series, sets the general expiration rule for all professional educator licenses (teacher, administrator, and student services personnel) issued by the Department of Public Instruction, which expire on June 30 of their set calendar year unless renewed, extended, or converted to another license type under SBE policy. It applies to every licensee and applicant holding or seeking a North Carolina professional educator license, and it serves as the baseline expiration timing that governs renewal and conversion procedures elsewhere in the series, such as those for Continuing Professional Licenses, Initial Professional Licenses, and Limited Licenses.
c34fed486a06288f: This section of LICN-003 (Licensing Testing Requirements) defines the key terms "Professional Educator," "Teacher," "Student Services Personnel," and "Administrator" used throughout the North Carolina educator licensure testing requirements, identifying which categories of school personnel (teachers, student services personnel, and administrators) must meet the NCSBE-mandated examination and pedagogy requirements for licensure.
933fcff281271208: This chunk (LICN-003 §3–§4) sets out the general testing requirements for individuals seeking a North Carolina professional educator's license, including the rule that an Initial Professional License can convert to a clear Continuing Professional License if the required State Board of Education exam is taken in the first year and passed by the third year. 26223d87c55c1376: This section of LICN-003 (Licensing Testing Requirements) introduces the NCSBE-approved testing table that sets out which examinations individuals seeking a North Carolina professional educator license (administrators, teachers, and student services personnel) must take, identifying Praxis test codes and required passing scores for each licensure area. d754ce792e663c1e: This chunk is part of LICN-003 §5's table of NCSBE-approved licensure testing requirements, specifically the Preschool/Elementary section, and it lists the exams and required scores for the Birth through Kindergarten (code 14) and Elementary K-6 (code 025) professional educator licenses. 910d5aa96f26251e: This chunk from LICN-003 §5 lists the required Praxis test codes and minimum passing scores for North Carolina Middle Grades (grades 6-9) teaching licensure in Language Arts, Mathematics, Science, and Social Studies, applying to educators seeking these license areas under the State Board of Education's approved testing requirements.
e746941d4f98fde8: This chunk is part of the LICN-003 Licensing Testing Requirements table under §5 of the North Carolina State Board of Education approved testing requirements, listing the Praxis exams and required passing scores for Secondary (grades 9-12) content-area teaching licenses, such as Biology, English, Mathematics, and Spanish. It applies to individuals seeking a North Carolina professional teaching license in these secondary subject areas, who must meet the listed test and score requirements to be licensed.
7362f4b8c6c777db: This chunk, from the Special Subject Areas (K-12) portion of the NCSBE-approved testing table in LICN-003 §5, lists the required ETS Praxis exams (or ACTFL OPI and WPT alternatives) and minimum passing scores for North Carolina special subject area licenses such as Art, Music, Health and Physical Education, Reading, Speech Communication, and world languages. 6634a1f341a0643a: This chunk is the tail of the LICN-003 table of NCSBE-approved licensure testing requirements, listing the required tests and passing scores for the Special Subject Areas (K-12) licenses, including World Languages such as Swahili, Turkish, and other foreign languages, and Safety and Driver Education. 15d24293b0a78d21: This chunk is part of the LICN-003 Licensing Testing Requirements table of NCSBE-approved examinations and required scores, specifically the Exceptional Children (K-12) licensure areas. b9523a2c44317121: This chunk is part of LICN-003 §5's table of NCSBE-approved testing requirements, listing the Praxis exam codes and required passing scores for North Carolina Career-Technical Education (grades 6-12) licensure areas, including Family & Consumer Sciences, Marketing Education, Technology Education, Business Education, and Computer Science & IT Education. 27eef16634f8564c: This chunk is part of the LICN-003 Licensing Testing Requirements table of NCSBE-approved examinations, and it specifies the required tests and minimum scores for North Carolina student services personnel licenses (School Counselor, School Psychologist, Media Coordinator, Audiologist, and Speech-Language Pathologist). 16d093029910800e: This chunk contains the footnotes to the LICN-003 testing table in Section 5, clarifying that the table covers only licensure areas with NCSBE-required examinations, that the Academically or Intellectually Gifted (AIG) license requires no test for completers of a recognized Educator Preparation Program (with the optional Praxis Gifted Education 5358 for others), that Career and Technical Education licensure is governed by a separate manual, and that any other world language with an ACTFL OPI is covered by the ACTFL testing option, applying to prospective North Carolina teachers seeking licensure by examination.
683d369b9a39ac92: This edTPA table within LICN-003 sets the passing and highly qualified score thresholds for the edTPA (Pearson) pedagogy assessment, which may fulfill the pedagogy assessment requirement for North Carolina professional educator licensure under Section 4. 658d3aadc1219196: This section of LICN-004 requires any applicant for a professional educator license to pay the application fee set out in LICN-008, as the final step after completing the application contents listed in Section 1. e49ffa35e31f8309: This chunk is part of LICN-006 Section I, which sets the rules for earning professional educator experience credit that determines salary for NC public school employees, and it specifically covers how full-time and part-time service in a school unit within a fiscal year (July 1 through June 30) translates into one year of credit, including the six-calendar-month requirement and the 15-hour-per-week minimum for part-time work.
abb8891cba448bd9: This chunk, part of Section I of LICN-006, sets the rules for how professional school experience is counted toward salary credit for NC public school educators, covering combining partial years, crediting service across multiple school units in one year, and calculating credit for college teaching by weekly class hours. 011dfba1606cdd0d: This chunk, part of Section I (Experience Credit as a Professional Educator) of NC State Board of Education policy LICN-006, sets out when tutoring, clerical paraprofessional, substitute, and leave-of-absence service does not count toward salary experience credit and when full-time instructional service performed on active military duty earns experience credit for North Carolina public school and charter school professional educators first employed on or after July 1, 2014. 943500a595a54aec: This chunk is part of LICN-006 §I(i), which awards one full year of professional experience credit to Master of School Administration (MSA) interns enrolled full-time in an approved educator preparation program who receive a stipend and complete a 10-month public school internship or an equivalent combination of internship and employment totaling the six-month employment requirement in an academic year.
6907ce8091fca193: This section of LICN-006 (Section II) sets out when non-teaching work experience may be credited toward a North Carolina educator's licensure experience rating for salary purposes, on recommendation by the employing LEA or charter school's personnel administrator. 9666ea07402622f4: This chunk, part of Section II of LICN-006, sets the rules for crediting relevant non-teaching work experience toward a professional educator's salary experience rating, including the full-time and half-time thresholds, the one-year-for-two or one-year-for-one conversion before and after a bachelor's degree, the Class V Career-Technical Trade and Industry Education provision, and the LEA and charter school repayment duty under G.S. 143-64.80 for improperly awarded credit.
420715ac77b712b5: This chunk is part of LICN-006 Section II, which governs non-teaching work experience credit toward a professional educator's licensure experience rating and sets out how the DPI Licensure Section decides, on a public school unit's recommendation, whether prior work experience is directly related to the educator's area of licensure or work assignment. 48ef2dc6a335f92e: This sub-item is the third of three factors DPI's Licensure Section weighs under LICN-006 §II when deciding whether to accept an LEA or charter school's recommendation to award non-teaching work experience credit toward a professional educator's salary experience rating. It specifically addresses whether specialized knowledge gained through prior non-teaching work, beyond what a traditional educator preparation program teaches, could enhance student learning.
ed2b59d55cc3da63: This section of LICN-006 governs experience credit for JROTC instructors, allowing up to 10 years of military experience toward salary when they have at least 20 years of service and military retirement, and directing those with fewer years to the non-teaching work experience criteria in Sections II and IV.
421c22074eba5c82: This section of LICN-006 (Section IV) governs non-teaching experience credit for military leadership roles, applying to veterans first employed by an NC LEA or charter school on or after July 1, 2014 who held commissioned, warrant, or non-commissioned officer leadership positions after completing formal military leadership training, with credit awarded at one year per two years of full-time leadership duty, on the employing LEA's recommendation, and excluding JROTC instructors (covered by Section III).
ce253e58ad35a9f0: This chunk sets out the first three eligibility criteria (accreditation, subject-area relevance to licensure or assignment, and a majority-of-day assignment requirement) that DPI uses to authorize graduate degree salary on the State salary schedule for professional educators holding a master's, doctoral, or other advanced degree not leading to a professional license. 64066f395e70ca59: This chunk sets out the eligibility conditions and review process for graduate degree salary authorization under Section V of LICN-006, covering the August 1, 2013 course deadline, the exemption for educators already receiving graduate pay before 2014-2015, the limitation to administrative, student services, and teaching positions, and the factors the DPI Licensure Section weighs when a public school unit recommends an educator's master's or doctoral degree for salary purposes.
816eafc35a506cea: This chunk sets out the first two of three factors the DPI Licensure Section weighs when deciding whether a public school unit's recommendation for graduate degree salary authorization under LICN-006 Section V should be accepted, namely curriculum alignment (a same-subject degree or at least 18 credit hours of aligned coursework) and transferable skills. 82c571baa1cd1129: This chunk is the third recommendation factor in Section V of LICN-006, which governs graduate degree salary authorization for professional educators in North Carolina public school units. 1db1f13269624dc2: This chunk is the appeals procedure within LICN-006 (Experience/Degree Credit for Salary Purposes), letting an LEA or charter school appeal the Licensure Section's rejection of a non-teaching work experience credit recommendation (Section II) or a graduate degree salary authorization (Section V) to the Superintendent of Public Instruction, who appoints a panel of at least three DPI staff whose majority decision is a final agency decision under G.S. 150B-2.
8437d90a548197e7: This Policy Statement introduces LICN-007, which governs SBE and Superintendent disciplinary sanctions (including suspension or revocation) and license application denials for professional educators (administrators, teachers, and student services personnel) licensed by DPI. 2d37bd6f31e2283e: This chunk opens LICN-007 by delegating the SBE's licensure disciplinary authority to the Superintendent of Public Instruction and defining key terms (child, conviction, license, local superintendent, professional educator, respondent, student) that govern the discipline and license denial process for North Carolina professional educators and license applicants. 056fcc4d33731357: This section of LICN-007 (Professional Educator Discipline) governs the Superintendent of Public Instruction's investigation of alleged misconduct by a professional educator licensee or license applicant, which is the first step before any license sanction or denial under Section 4. 30e4b6deddf87d41: This chunk sets out the notice-and-appeal step of LICN-007's disciplinary process, in which the Superintendent of Public Instruction issues a proposed order to a licensed professional educator or license applicant after finding cause for sanction or denial under Section 4, and the respondent then has 60 days from electronic delivery or USPS mailing to commence a Chapter 150B, Article 3 contested case or the proposed order becomes final.
feb2c0fb5bc2b0fd: This subsection of LICN-007 Section 3 (Investigation of Alleged Misconduct) governs what happens after the Superintendent of Public Instruction issues a proposed order to sanction or deny a professional educator's license: it stays the order if the respondent (a current licensee or license applicant) timely files an administrative contested case under G.S. 150B, and otherwise makes the order final for enforcement after the 60-day deadline.
9f249227f0b069ad: This section of LICN-007 (Section 4, Denying or Sanctioning a License) lists the grounds on which the Superintendent of Public Instruction may impose discipline on a current professional educator license holder or deny a license application after investigation, including fraud in an application, criminal convictions, dismissal or forced resignation from a PSU, out-of-state license revocation, failure to report suspected child abuse, Testing Code of Ethics violations, and other unethical or unprofessional conduct under the Standards of Professional Conduct, EVAL-035.
ffbace1331ccb734: This chunk is Section 4(b)-(c) of LICN-007, Professional Educator Discipline, and sets out the seven factors the Superintendent must weigh (such as the relationship between the misconduct and the educator's professional duties, its severity and impact on students, culpability, remorse, reform, and risk of recidivism) before imposing discipline on a professional educator's license or denying a license application, and directs that sanctions against a current licensee then follow Section 5.
c9332b4e2bf4d429: This section of LICN-007 (Professional Educator Discipline) lists the sanctions the Superintendent may impose on a licensed professional educator (administrator, teacher, or student services personnel) after finding grounds under Section 4, including written warning, written reprimand, suspension for a defined term, and revocation, plus optional remedial conditions and the summary suspension procedure for emergencies or pending criminal charges that would trigger automatic revocation under G.S. 115C-270.35(b).
a7e86ac5ce2df4cd: This provision, within Section 5 (Disciplinary Sanctions) of LICN-007, governs how DPI publicizes and reports discipline imposed on a professional educator's license, including publication on its website and reporting to NASDTEC once the 60-day period to contest a proposed order under Section 3 has expired, with the exception of Written Warnings and limits on disclosing confidential information.
69138c8aa17de345: This chunk is Section 6 of LICN-007, the Automatic Revocation provision, which requires the Superintendent to revoke a professional educator's license without a hearing upon verified proof of a guilty or nolo contendere plea or final conviction for any of the enumerated crimes, such as murder, sexual offenses, child abuse, and prostitution involving minors. b6d7ff569481d22a: This subsection sets the notice procedure that governs automatic revocation under LICN-007 §6(a), applying to professional educators whose criminal record shows a guilty or nolo contendere plea or final conviction for an enumerated offense such as murder, sexual offenses, or child abuse. 016fc25fd291f991: This section of LICN-007 (Professional Educator Discipline) governs the voluntary surrender of a professional educator license issued under G.S. 24d9338aeb39e527: This section of LICN-007 governs how an individual whose professional educator license was revoked, or whose license application was denied, under the Policy may petition the Superintendent of Public Instruction for reinstatement or reconsideration no sooner than 12 months after the revocation or denial, including the written petition contents and the Superintendent's options to deny, grant, or grant on probation with a one-year review.
22380d6c3dbe3323: This chunk, part of LICN-007 Section 9, sets out the mandatory reporting duties of PSU administrators (such as superintendents, principals, and personnel administrators) who learn of misconduct by a licensed professional educator that leads to suspension without pay, termination, non-renewal, or resignation, requiring written notice to the Superintendent of Public Instruction within five calendar days. f190b9be6de7f979: This chunk sets out the general framework for LICN-012 student services personnel licenses, covering the five license classifications (School Counselor, School Social Worker, School Psychologist, Media Coordinator, and Instructional Technology Specialist-Telecommunications) and the baseline requirement that applicants complete an educator preparation program at the Master's, Specialist, or Doctoral level. It also limits each applicant to the license matching the highest degree level at which they completed an EPP, while noting that such applicants may still qualify for graduate salary pay under LICN-006.
04d4df1d8a7627d2: This chunk sets out the degree-level and credential requirements for three student services personnel licenses under LICN-012: school social worker (bachelor's level or higher), school psychologist (specialist or doctoral level, with NCSP certification conferring a continuing professional license), and school audiologist (doctoral audiology degree plus an NCBOESLPA audiology license, with a grandfather exemption for master's degrees obtained before October 1, 2007). It applies to applicants seeking these specific student services personnel licenses from the Department of Public Instruction.
e914018cac7ad233: This chunk sets out the degree and licensing requirements for school speech-language pathologists (§8) and the examination timing rules for student services personnel licenses (§9), including when a continuing versus initial professional license is issued to applicants under LICN-012.
1dbc7cb5120656a5: This section of LICN-013 governs how an applicant may add a new teaching license area to an existing Initial Professional License (IPL) or Continuing Professional License (CPL), either by passing the applicable licensure exam or by completing 24 credit hours of coursework with grades of C or better, with Elementary Education and Exceptional Children: General Curriculum restricted to the examination route only.
79aea6bb2e8c1c7e: This section of LICN-013 (Add-On Teaching Areas) bars the Department of Public Instruction from adding new teaching license areas under Section 1 to certain restricted or temporary license classifications, including the Permit to Teach, Emergency, Residency, Limited, Provisional, International Faculty, and Career and Technical Education – Restricted licenses. It applies to educators holding these license types who seek to add a license area to their credentials through coursework or licensure examinations.
1382ada6898fd67f: This chunk from LICN-017 (Permit to Teach) sets out who may request a North Carolina permit to teach, which is available only to applicants who hold at least a bachelor's degree and have never held another North Carolina professional educator license, along with the permit's June 30 expiration, its non-renewable status, and its pay-scale placement at the A-Level with zero years of experience. It applies to public school unit governing bodies requesting permits for applicants they plan to employ.
851ed7d67c357aa9: This chunk sets out the eligibility requirements and validity period for an emergency license, which a public-school unit's governing body may request for an applicant it has hired who holds a bachelor's degree with at least 18 relevant credit hours, has not completed an approved educator preparation program in that area, and does not qualify for a residency license. It also bars anyone who holds or previously held a residency license in the same area from receiving an emergency license, and limits each emergency license to validity through June 30 of the requested fiscal year with no extension or renewal.
85d1afc30b63f769: This section of LICN-018 governs salary placement for teachers holding an emergency license, providing that they are paid at the A-Level (bachelor's degree) step of the State Salary Schedule while remaining eligible for graduate degree pay or experience pay under LICN-006. It applies to applicants who have been granted an emergency license under this policy and addresses how that license is certified for pay purposes.
8e99425dcc976da4: This section of LICN-019 sets out who may be requested for a residency license and when eligibility applies, covering the coursework (24 hours) or licensure exam pathways for public school units and eligible nonpublic schools hiring applicants, the bar on holding a residency license in a license area where a permit or emergency license is also sought, and the path for former lateral entry license holders who never converted their license to a continuing professional license.
e4da88618c026a91: This section of LICN-019 sets out the renewal requirements for a residency license, including the documentation a public school unit or eligible nonpublic school must submit to DPI for a teacher to renew in the second and third years, and the conditions under which an expired residency license may be reinstated for an applicant hired within three years of the initial effective date.
bfca07bec9c7774f: This section of LICN-019 governs how a holder of a residency license converts to an initial or continuing professional license (IPL or CPL), including the LICN-020 and LICN-024 requirements, EPP recommendation, and the July 1 effective-date rule tied to the third-year June 30 deadline. It also covers requesting a residency license in an additional license area for an applicant who already holds a clear license in another area, as requested by a public school unit or eligible nonpublic school employing the applicant.
2a303f55e54dd20d: This section of LICN-019 sets out the professional development and field experience a public school unit must provide to a teacher holding a residency license during the first year, including at least three hours of pre-classroom field experience, 10 hours over the year, and ten days of required training topics such as school policies, the Standard Course of Study, EVAAS, lesson planning, classroom management, and services for children with disabilities. It applies to PSUs that employ residency licensees and is a mandatory precondition tied to renewal under Section 2 of the policy.
ccd1f8943a9c78cc: This alternative professional development pathway under LICN-019 §5(d) lets a public school unit satisfy the Section 5(a) requirements for teachers holding a residency license, emergency license, or permit to teach by providing specified trainings, including at least eight hours of training before the teacher begins classroom teaching. It applies to PSUs that employ such teachers and is part of the broader professional development requirements for residency license holders.
4007ef9c66f6a9f7: This subsection of LICN-019 (Residency License), within the professional development requirements of Section 5, allows a public school unit employing a residency license teacher to schedule the 10 required professional development days either entirely in the preservice period before classroom teaching begins or split them, with five in preservice and five during the teacher's first year on the residency license. It applies to public school units (PSUs) that employ teachers holding residency licenses under G.S. 115C-270.20 and 16 NCAC 06C .0338.
a36089ac6b2d3364: This chunk sets out the eligibility pathways for an Initial Professional License (IPL) in LICN-020, covering applicants who completed a North Carolina or out-of-state educator preparation program or who hold an out-of-state clear license with fewer than three years of teaching experience, and it allows a public school unit's governing body to request an IPL for an employee who has finished all EPP requirements but not the licensure exam.
d383d2b5534907e0: This section of LICN-020 (Initial Professional License) states that an Initial Professional License (IPL), issued to applicants who meet the qualification requirements in §1 or the school-unit request provision in §2, authorizes the licensee to work as an independent professional educator in North Carolina. It applies to individuals granted an initial professional educator license, such as graduates of North Carolina or out-of-state educator preparation programs and applicants with prior out-of-state clear licenses.
49a042c62c56d4c8: This section of LICN-023 sets out the qualifications for obtaining a limited teaching license, covering both applicants a public school unit requests under G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(4a) and former lateral entry license holders who have not yet passed the licensure exam for an IPL or CPL. It applies to current PSU employees and requires an affidavit from the local superintendent and the applicant's principal certifying effectiveness and a commitment to encourage pursuit of an IPL or CPL.
5318d598540227ab: This chunk, from LICN-023 §2 on limited license renewal, sets out the two requirements a public school unit (PSU) and its employed licensee must meet to renew a limited teaching license: a supervising principal and local superintendent affidavit confirming current employment, effective teaching, and encouragement to pursue a CPL, and a demonstration that the licensee met or exceeded expected EVAAS growth, excluding the 2019-2020 and 2020-2021 school years.
d0e44f02a53784ca: This section of LICN-023 addresses portability of a limited license, which generally cannot be transferred from one public school unit to another, with an exception for military service members and spouses governed by LICN-028. It applies to individuals holding a limited license issued under this policy and to the PSUs that employ them.
dae771022db2ead5: This section of LICN-024 sets out the requirements a teacher must meet to obtain a continuing professional teacher license in North Carolina, including holding an initial professional educator or residency license, meeting licensure examination requirements, completing three years of licensed teaching experience, and finishing a Beginning Teacher Support Program under TCED-016 (with exceptions for applicants with three years of out-of-state licensed teaching experience or those who previously held a CPL that reverted to an IPL). It applies to teacher applicants seeking to advance from an initial professional educator license to a continuing professional license.
a0b5b00f400ec49f: LICN-024 §2 sets the examination timing and other requirements for obtaining a continuing professional administrator or student services personnel license, while §3 through §5 cover CPL eligibility through a clear out-of-state license, the practice rights a CPL confers, and how long a CPL remains in effect after retirement. This chunk applies to North Carolina applicants for administrator or student services personnel CPLs and to licensees holding a CPL.
c5f62713d67ee597: This section of LICN-025 sets out how out-of-state applicants with fewer than three years of licensed professional educator experience qualify for a North Carolina Initial Professional License (IPL), including the two eligibility routes (holding an out-of-state license in a corresponding area or completing a recognized educator preparation program) and the timing requirements for satisfying North Carolina licensure examinations, which differ for Elementary Education and Special Education: General Curriculum versus other license areas.
74bd18f5dd9050fa: This section of LICN-025 sets out the requirements for an out-of-state applicant with more than three years of licensed professional educator experience to obtain a North Carolina Continuing Professional License (CPL), including the need to hold a clear out-of-state license and either a National Board for Professional Teaching Standards certification or licensure requirements substantially similar to North Carolina's (completion of a recognized educator preparation program and a passing out-of-state exam in each license area sought under LICN-010).
6b5b8027781439f9: This section of LICN-025 governs how out-of-state applicants use passing out-of-state exam results to obtain an initial professional license (IPL) or continuing professional license (CPL) in North Carolina, and to add a teaching license area at initial application, and it directs applicants who seek to add an area after receiving a North Carolina license to follow LICN-013 instead.
da121d5e2a5d73a3: This section of LICN-026 sets out the eligibility requirements, issuance limits, and extension process for the international faculty license, which applies to foreign nationals holding a J-1 cultural exchange visa who do not qualify for any other DPI license. It requires that the applicant be supported by a DPI-approved sponsor, that the license be issued only at the sponsor's request, and that it be extended (but not renewed) for two years at the joint request of the sponsor and the employing public school unit's governing body while the J-1 visa remains active.
a6a41880ac5c2069: This chunk addresses how an international faculty license (for J-1 visa holders sponsored under LICN-026) is treated for pay purposes and conversion: it is placed at the A-Level bachelor's-degree rate with zero years of experience for State Salary Schedule certification, while licensees may accumulate PSU teaching years toward future pay, and the license cannot be converted to another license type until it expires.
548ff00d010dd08d: This chunk from LICN-027 (Lifetime License) explains how a current continuing professional license (CPL) holder may request conversion to a lifetime license from the Department of Public Instruction, based on 30 or more years of creditable NCTSERS service or 30 or more years of combined experience as a licensed teacher, administrator, or student services personnel in North Carolina PSUs. It also states that such applicants are exempt from completing continuing education credits for the renewal period immediately before conversion, while PSUs may still require lifetime license holders to complete professional development as a condition of employment.
6bb1a8436bf2fa32: This section of LICN-027 (Lifetime License) establishes that a lifetime license converted from a continuing professional license under §1 remains valid for the licensee's natural life, subject only to suspension or revocation under LICN-007. It applies to North Carolina educators, administrators, and student services personnel who have been granted a lifetime license based on 30 or more years of creditable NCTSS service or combined PSU experience.
d22dbbe9f233ae29: This chunk belongs to LICN-028, the policy on special professional educator licensure provisions for active-duty servicemembers and their spouses, and its definitions section establishes who qualifies (servicemembers across the armed forces, NOAA and Public Health Service commissioned corps) and what counts as a "covered license" (one in good standing, not revoked or disciplined, with no pending unprofessional-conduct investigation, and not surrendered under investigation). These definitions frame the eligibility criteria used in the later sections on recognizing out-of-state licenses and employment in North Carolina public school units.
09d109464d6e73bc: This chunk, within LICN-028 on special license provisions for active-duty servicemembers and their spouses, incorporates 10 U.S.C. 101 and Chapter 50 of Title 50 by reference and sets out the two ways an active-duty servicemember stationed in North Carolina, or that servicemember's spouse, may be employed in a license-required position at a public school unit and paid on the State Salary Schedule: either by applying for a North Carolina professional educator license under State Board of Education policy, or by obtaining recognition of a covered out-of-state license under the Veterans Auto and Education Improvement Act of 2022.
0699ea3432d86c35: This chunk is §4(a) of LICN-028, which sets out how a servicemember or their spouse who holds a covered out-of-state professional educator license can obtain North Carolina recognition of that license after relocating to the state on military orders, and lists the documents and notarized affidavit the application must include. Note that its clause (iii)(D) cross-references "Subsection 3(a)(iii)(C)," which appears to be a misreference to §4(a)(iii)(C).
50b1fce1b756ceea: This chunk, part of LICN-028's provisions for active-duty servicemembers and their spouses, governs how long the Department of Public Instruction must recognize an out-of-state covered professional educator license after a servicemember relocates to North Carolina on military orders, and it allows out-of-state exam scores submitted with a North Carolina license application to come from a jurisdiction other than where the applicant completed their EPP or APP.
c53be84b73ce25c0: This chunk, from Section 5 of LICN-028 (Special License Provisions for Active-Duty Servicemembers and Spouses), explains that a servicemember or spouse pursuing a North Carolina residency license under LICN-019 has the three-year EPP and IPL/CPL timeframe held in abeyance if military orders take them outside the state until they return to North Carolina and resume employment in a public school. Section 6 addresses limited licenses, providing that a servicemember or spouse holding a limited license who relocates within North Carolina on military orders and takes a job with a different local board of education keeps that license valid for the new assignment.
e8604d8727c7ec8c: This chunk is part of LICN-030, the North Carolina policy on renewing a continuing professional license (CPL) every five years, and it sets the continuing education unit (CEU) requirements for teachers. It specifies the eight-CEU composition for teachers in Pre-Kindergarten through Grade 5 (three license-area, three literacy, and two general CEUs) and for teachers in Grades 6 through 12 (four license-area and four general CEUs).
04877d2dc50d02f1: This section of LICN-030 sets the annual-evaluation requirement for renewing a continuing professional license (CPL), applying to teachers employed by a local board of education who must show a "proficient" rating (three of five NC Professional Teaching Standards, including Standard 4) on their most recent evaluation in NCEES. It also requires all teachers to maintain a professional development plan aligned with the Professional Teaching Standards.
eb715455196e5db1: This chunk, part of LICN-030 (License Renewal for Teachers), governs the renewal of a continuing professional license (CPL) for teachers employed by a local board of education who were not rated proficient on their most recent annual evaluation, allowing the local school administrative unit to place them on a mandatory improvement plan that leads to an initial professional license (IPL) instead of expiration. It sets the plan's length (60 or 90 instructional days depending on whether the school is low performing), the conditions for later reapplying for a CPL, and the rule that reverting to an IPL does not constitute a demotion or salary reduction.
abecfc37396b6b46: This section, LICN-030 §3, is the General Assembly member exemption to the continuing education requirements for renewing a teacher's continuing professional license (CPL) under LICN-030. It applies to members of the North Carolina General Assembly who serve any portion of a term during a renewal cycle, provided they notify the Department of Public Instruction of the exemption during that cycle.
f2b56b0626b3e35e: This chunk, part of LICN-031 on license renewal for administrators, sets out the requirement that administrator license holders must renew every five years by completing eight continuing education units (CEUs), including four focused on instruction, human resources, and management and four general CEUs relevant to the K-12 educational environment.
f69f4f17aa374b44: This chunk from LICN-032 sets out the license renewal requirements for student services personnel, who must renew their continuing professional license every five years by completing eight CEUs (four aligned with EVAL discipline standards and four general K-12-related CEUs). It also exempts school audiologists and school speech-language pathologists from these continuing education requirements as long as they continue to meet the applicable LICN-012 requirements.
91f4693a6c93b19d: This chunk, part of the general license renewal requirements (LICN-033), covers how professional educators earn continuing education units (CEUs) through college coursework, professional development, and National Board Certification credit, and how an expired continuing professional license (CPL) may be validated by the Department of Public Instruction at the request of a public school unit's governing body. It applies to licensed professional educators, particularly teachers seeking renewal, and to PSU governing bodies requesting validation for applicants they employ.
dc0e91a1184979f0: This section of LICN-033, General License Renewal Requirements, explains when hours spent in mandatory training programs count toward a professional educator's continuing education credits for renewing a continuing professional license, and it sets out public school unit responsibilities for approving renewal activities and adding local continuing education requirements. It applies to licensed professional educators employed by public school units and to the governing bodies and local boards of education that oversee those units.
